notes: Dev-split ABox revision (all determinate, no worlds): the photon has spin 1/2 (has_spin, functional). The one related question asks whether the photon is a boson, which the spin-statistics rule overturns; a model that keeps it holds a boson with half-integer spin, which no world allows. A second stored route back, recorded as residual risk: the photon is a gauge boson and gauge bosons have spin 1; after the edit that class rule must give way for the photon, and either way the photon has half-integer spin. Consequences for lasers and Bose-Einstein statistics move with the same rule and no query asks them. Derived: the Pauli principle (inheritance), whether the photon has the same spin as the particles the Dirac equation describes (composition: a stored fact about the Dirac equation, asked as a spin comparison because a massless spin-1/2 particle would be described by a Weyl rather than the Dirac equation), and the spin of "the quantum of light" (binding, a description the model holds separately that carries no class rule fixing spin). The near unrelated question asks the Higgs boson's spin (0), which shares the relation and differs from the new answer (the electron was not used because its spin equals the new answer).
